([[Montverde, Florida]]) | college = [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] (2022–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 17 | draft_team = [[Los Angeles Lakers]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–{{nbay|2024|end}} | team1 = [[Los Angeles Lakers]] | years2 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023]]–[[2024–25 NBA G League season|2024]] | team2 = →[[South Bay Lakers]] | years3 = {{nbay|2024|end}} | team3 = [[Philadelphia 76ers]] | years4 = [[2024–25 NBA G League season|2025]] | team4 = →[[Delaware Blue Coats]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA In-Season Tournament champions|NBA Cup champion]] ([[2023 NBA In-Season Tournament championship game|2023]]) * [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big Ten Freshman of the Year]] (2023) * [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] All-Freshman Team (2023) * Second-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] (2023) }} '''Jalen Hood-Schifino''' ({{IPAc-en|ˈ|h|ʊ|d|_|ʃ|ɪ|ˈ|f|iː|n|oʊ}} {{respelling|HUUD|_|shif|EE|noh}};{{cite press release|title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide|url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide|website=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2023|access-date=May 18, 2024}} born June 19, 2003) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]]. He was a five-star and four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class. ==High school career== Hood-Schifino played for three different programs in high school. He began his prep career at [[Northside Christian Academy]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]]. As a sophomore, Hood-Schifino played at Combine Academy in [[Lincolnton, North Carolina]]. Before his junior season, Hood-Schifino transferred to national powerhouse [[Montverde Academy]] in Florida, coached by Kevin Boyle. At Montverde, Hood-Schifino won back-to-back [[High School Showcase|GEICO High School Basketball National titles]] (2021 and 2022). Hood-Schifino was named an all-star and invited to play in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], where he scored 14 points and hit three three-point shots. In the off-season, prior to college he also played for coach Norton Hurd IV and Team Thad, an AAU program founded by NBA player [[Thaddeus Young]]. He spent time working out in [[California]] with professionals, including the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]’ [[Paul George]]. Hood-Schifino stated that his time at Montverde prepared him for college basketball, noting, "The everyday grind at Montverde, people don’t really know what’s, you know, put into it, like the practices. It's almost like a college practice; you're practicing three-plus hours every day, so it really prepared me for now. . . Now going through college, it’s almost like I’m at Montverde but at a college level." ===Recruiting=== While playing at the Combine Academy, Hood-Schifino committed to play for [[Jeff Capel]] and [[Pittsburgh Panthers men's basketball|Pittsburgh]]. At the time, it was considered a major recruiting win for the Panthers to land Hood-Schifino, a Pittsburgh native. But following Hood-Schifino's sophomore year in high school, he chose to reopen his recruitment. The [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]] became involved in Hood-Schifino's recruitment in the summer of 2021, just months after head coach [[Mike Woodson]] began in Bloomington. Hood-Schifino committed to the Hoosiers in August 2021. He was the highest-rated recruit to sign with the Hoosiers since [[Romeo Langford]] in 2018 and the 9th highest-ranked recruit for the program since 1998. {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2022}} {{College athlete recruit entry | recruit = Jalen Hood-Schifino | position = [[Point guard|PG]] / [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania|Pittsburgh, PA]] | highschool = [[Montverde Academy]] (FL) | feet = 6 | inches = 6 | weight = 215 | 40 = | commitdate = August 24, 2021 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 4 | espn stars = 4 | espn grade = 89 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2022 | rivals ref title = Indiana 2022 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2022 Indiana Hoosiers Recruiting Class | 247 ref title = | rivals school = indiana | 247 school = | espn schoolid = 84 | scout overall = | rivals overall = 18 | 247 overall = 26 | espn overall = 26 | accessdate = October 19, 2022 | bball = yes }} ==College career== Prior to Hood-Schifino's freshman year with the Hoosiers, a mock NBA draft projected him as a first-round pick. A panel of Big Ten media named him the preseason freshman of the year in the league.{{cite news |last1=Bozich |first1=Alex |title=2022-23 Indiana basketball player profile: Jalen Hood-Schifino |url=https://www.insidethehall.com/2022/10/17/2022-23-indiana-basketball-player-profile-jalen-hood-schifino/ |access-date=October 19, 2022 |agency=Inside the Hall}} In his [[2022–23 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|lone season]] at Indiana, Hood-Schifino was named [[Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Big Ten Freshman of the Year]] and third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] by the coaches and media. In 32 games (32 starts), he averaged 13.5 points, 4.1 rebounds, and 3.7 assists in 33.1 minutes per game. On January 8, 2023, Hood-Schifino scored 33 points in an 84–83 loss against [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]] at [[Simon Skjodt Assembly Hall|Assembly Hall]], the most points by a freshman at Indiana since [[Eric Gordon]] against [[Chattanooga Mocs men's basketball|Chattanooga]] in 2007. On February 25, 2023, Hood-Schifino scored an Indiana freshman-record 35 points in a 79–71 win against [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] at [[Mackey Arena]]. On March 31, 2023, Hood-Schifino declared for the [[NBA draft]], foregoing his final three years of college eligibility. ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles Lakers (2023–2025)=== The [[Los Angeles Lakers]] selected Hood-Schifino with the 17th overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|first=Paolo|last=Songco|title=Kobe Bryant fan Jalen Hood-Schifino reacts to going No. 17 to Lakers in 2023 NBA Draft|url=https://clutchpoints.com/lakers-kobe-bryant-fan-jalen-hood-schifino-reacts-to-going-no-17|website=ClutchPoints.com|date=June 22, 2023|access-date=June 22, 2023}} Throughout his rookie and sophomore seasons, Hood-Schifino was [[NBA G League#Standard assignment|assigned]] several times to the [[South Bay Lakers]]{{cite web|title=2023-2024 South Bay Lakers Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/South-Bay-Lakers/12/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 17, 2024}}{{cite web|title=2024-2025 South Bay Lakers Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/gleague/teams/South-Bay-Lakers/12/Transaction_History/2025|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 17, 2024}} and on November 27, 2023, he made his NBA debut for the Lakers in a 138–94 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. On March 21, 2024, Hood-Schifino underwent a lumbar [[discectomy|microdiscectomy]] procedure, with an unknown timetable for his return.{{cite web|title=Lakers News: Jalen Hood-Schifino Undergoes Surgery on Back Injury; Timetable TBD|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10113967-lakers-news-jalen-hood-schifino-undergoes-surgery-on-back-injury-timetable-tbd|website=BleacherReport.com|access-date=March 21, 2024}} On February 2, 2025, Hood-Schifino was traded, alongside a 2025 second round pick from the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and another from the [[Dallas Mavericks]], to the [[Utah Jazz]] as part of [[Luka Dončić trade|a deal]] that sent [[Luka Dončić]], [[Maxi Kleber]], [[Markieff Morris]] and cash to the Lakers while sending [[Max Christie]], [[Anthony Davis]], a 2029 first-round pick and cash considerations to the Mavericks.{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Acquire Jalen Hood-Schifino and Two Future Second-Round Picks|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-acquire-jalen-hood-schifino-and-two-future-second-round-picks|website=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2025|access-date=February 4, 2025}} On February 7, he was waived by the Jazz without appearing in a game.{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz Waive Jalen Hood-Schifino|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-waive-jalen-hood-schifino|website=NBA.com|date=February 7, 2025|access-date=February 7, 2025}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2025)=== On February 28, 2025, Hood-Schifino signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |date=2025-03-01 |title=Philadelphia 76ers’ surprising change of game, signing former Lakers’ pick Jalen Hood-Schifino, foreshadows David Ro |url=https://motociclismo.pt/en/philadelphia-76ers-surprising-change-of-game-signing-former-lakers-pick-jalen-hood-schifino-foreshadows-david-roddys-departure/ |access-date=2025-03-01 |website=Motociclismo |language=en-GB}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2023}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2023–24 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A. He also attended [[Gateway School District]] until he moved. Growing up, he played basketball in his grandparents' backyard and played against his older cousins, Sherron and DeAndre Schifino. DeAndre would end up being a member of the University of Pittsburgh's football team. Sherron Schifino would end up playing college basketball. Sherron and DeAndre Schifino's friends — who were also older than Hood-Schifino — played with them, too. "I was always the young kid," Hood-Schifino later explained.{{cite news |last1=Tachmann |first1=Tyler |title=Jalen Hood-Schifino brings competitiveness, versatility to Indiana |url=https://www.insidethehall.com/2022/06/24/jalen-hood-schifino-brings-competitiveness-versatility-to-indiana/ |access-date=October 19, 2022 |agency=Inside the Hall |date=June 24, 2022}} As part of a [[student athlete compensation]] package to raise awareness for Indiana charity partners, Hood-Schifino endorsed Big Brothers Big Sisters of Central Indiana, offering in-person appearances (such as speaking, presentation of skills, autograph sessions, and the like) as well as social media posts promoting these appearances and the charity.{{cite news |title=11 IU basketball athletes join summer class for Hoosiers For Good NIL deal |url=https://www.insidethehall.com/2022/08/03/11-iu-basketball-athletes-join-summer-class-for-hoosiers-for-good-nil-deal/ |access-date=October 19, 2022 |agency=Inside the Hall |date=August 3, 2022}} His uncle Drew{{Cite web |last=John |first=Andrew |date=July 4, 2019 |title=Former Penn Hills athlete Jalen Hood-Schifino gains college attention on summer circuit |url=https://tribhssn.triblive.com/former-penn-hills-athlete-jalen-hood-schifino-gains-college-attention-on-summer-circuit/ |access-date=June 27, 2023 |website=Trib HSSN |language=en}} played college basketball for the [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia Mountaineers]]{{Cite web |title=Drew Schifino - Men's Basketball |url=https://wvusports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/drew-schifino/12684 |access-date=June 27, 2023 |website=West Virginia University Athletics |language=en}} and the [[California Vulcans]],{{Cite web |date=January 18, 2005 |title=Schifino ruled ineligible at California (Pa.) |url=https://archive.triblive.com/news/schifino-ruled-ineligible-at-california-pa/ |access-date=June 27, 2023 |website=Pittsburgh Tribune-Review}} before embarking on a professional career.{{Cite web |title=Drew Schifino |url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Drew-Schifino/46214 |access-date=June 27, 2023 |website=Eurobasket.com}} Another uncle, [[Jake Schifino]], played in the [[National Football League|NFL]] for the [[Tennessee Titans]].{{Cite web |last=Teaford |first=Elliott |date=June 23, 2023 |title=NBA draft: Lakers take Indiana guard Jalen Hood-Schifino with 1st-round pick |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2023/06/22/lakers-take-indiana-pg-jalen-hood-schifino-with-1st-round-pick-in-nba-draft/ |access-date=June 27, 2023 |website=Orange County Register |language=en-US}} ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *{{basketballstats}} *[https://iuhoosiers.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jalen-hood-schifino/16673 Indiana Hoosiers bio] {{navboxes|list= {{Los Angeles Lakers 2023 NBA Cup champions}} {{2023 NBA draft}} }} {{DEFAULTSORT:Hood-Schifino, Jalen}} [[Category:2003 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:21st-century American sportsmen]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:Basketball players from Pittsburgh]] [[Category:Delaware Blue Coats players]] [[Category:Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball players]] [[Category:Los Angeles Lakers draft picks]] [[Category:Los Angeles Lakers players]] [[Category:Montverde Academy alumni]] [[Category:Philadelphia 76ers players]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:South Bay Lakers players]]
